children.text: A fall can seem minor yet still leave lasting damage. In Colorado, injuries following a backward fall commonly include muscle strains and sprains, herniated discs, spinal compression fractures, and trauma to the spinal cord itself. Depending on severity, an injured person may face persistent pain, limited mobility, numbness, or paralysis.
Knowing the
symptoms to look for after a fall on the back
matters, particularly when the spine bears the brunt of the impact, since some warning signs appear right away, while others take hours or days to surface. Our experienced

team

help Denver residents injured in falls, including those on icy walkways, uneven staircases, or slick flooring, pursue the compensation they need for their recovery.
What to Look for After Falling on Your Back

Not every injury announces itself right away. Shock and adrenaline can mask pain in the moments after a fall, so the body deserves a careful check both immediately and again several hours later. Some people feel fine at first, only to notice stiffness, nerve-related sensations, or a dull ache in the lower back by the next day, and those delayed signs often carry as much weight as the ones that appear instantly.

The 24 to 72 hours after a fall matter as much as the moment itself. Pain that spreads, swelling that will not fade, or weakness that limits movement can all point to damage sitting beneath the surface, even when nothing seems seriously wrong. Recognizing these signs early, from pain and visible swelling to changes in sensation, balance, and mental clarity, often makes the difference between a fast recovery and a missed diagnosis.
Severe Pain

Certain symptoms signal possible spinal cord involvement and warrant urgent care, including numbness, tingling, or weakness in the limbs, loss of bladder or bowel control, or difficulty standing. Pain that limits movement, worsens over time, or resists rest deserves prompt evaluation rather than medication alone, and often extends to the neck next.
Neck Pain
A fall onto the back can snap the head forward and back, straining the neck the way whiplash does.
MedlinePlus

notes neck injuries may involve the muscles, ligaments, or discs of the cervical spine, with symptoms sometimes surfacing the next day. Stiffness radiating into the shoulders should never be dismissed as routine soreness, particularly when it reaches the head.
Headaches

Headaches following a fall, particularly at the base of the skull, often indicate whiplash or a mild concussion rather than ordinary tension. A headache that worsens with movement or persists beyond a day warrants evaluation.
Dizziness or Nausea

Dizziness or nausea after a fall can signal a head injury even without a direct blow, since impact can jolt the brain inside the skull. Anyone feeling lightheaded, unsteady, or nauseated afterward should seek medical attention rather than wait, especially if they are also experiencing mental fog.
Confusion or Memory Loss

Confusion, trouble concentrating, or gaps in memory after a fall can indicate a concussion or, in serious cases, bleeding inside the skull. These changes sometimes develop gradually, so anyone unusually foggy should be evaluated promptly rather than monitored at home.
Bruising and Swelling

Bruising and swelling over the spine, shoulder blades, or tailbone rank among the most visible symptoms to look for after a fall on the back, though large or spreading bruises can signal more than surface damage.
MedlinePlus
explains that bruises form when blood leaks out of small blood vessels under the skin, and go away in about two weeks. An expanding bruise or notable swelling may indicate damage beneath the surface.
Difficulty with Movement and Balance

Difficulty walking, standing up from a seated position, or maintaining balance after a fall suggests something beyond ordinary soreness. Weakness in one or both legs, limping, or leaning on furniture for support can signal spinal cord compression, nerve damage, or a fracture requiring immediate treatment. This weakness often begins as tingling, a symptom easy to dismiss at first.
Weakness, Tingling, Numbness, or Stiffness
These sensations in the back, buttocks, or legs often signal nerve compression from a herniated disc, fractured vertebra, or other spinal injury. The
common back injuries after a fall
range from strains and sprains to compression fractures and spinal cord trauma, and knowing which one is behind the symptoms guides the right treatment.
Loss of Bowel or Bladder Control

Loss of bowel or bladder control after a fall is one of the clearest signs of a medical emergency, sometimes pointing to cauda equina syndrome, where nerves at the base of the spinal cord become compressed and stop signaling correctly, risking permanent damage or paralysis if untreated. Anyone with sudden incontinence, groin numbness, or leg weakness should go to the emergency room immediately.

children.text: Common Back Injuries

Falls affect the spine in distinct ways, and the severity of harm often depends on the force of impact and the angle at which someone lands. Our Denver attorneys most often see four injuries follow a fall: strains and sprains, herniated discs, compression fractures, and spinal cord trauma, each carrying its own risks and warning signs. Understanding what sets these conditions apart helps injured individuals recognize what they may be dealing with and why prompt medical evaluation matters.
Muscle Strains and Sprains
Among the most frequent back injuries caused by a fall are
muscle strains
and sprains. These involve overstretching or tearing muscles, ligaments, or tendons in the back. Victims often feel pain, tightness, or reduced mobility shortly after the incident.
Herniated Discs

When a fall puts too much pressure on the spine, the discs between the vertebrae can shift or rupture. This may irritate surrounding nerves and trigger pain, tingling, or weakness in the legs. It can be especially uncomfortable when sitting or bending.
Compression Fractures

Falls can also cause the small bones in your spine, called vertebrae, to compress. This condition is particularly common in older adults. Tingling, back spasms, and persistent pain may follow, sometimes worsening with movement.
Spinal Cord Injuries

In more serious situations, a fall can damage the spinal cord itself. These types of injuries may affect sensation, movement, or internal control functions and can lead to partial or total paralysis in extreme cases. They often need immediate and ongoing medical care.
Important Considerations

Not every fall produces the same outcome, and several factors shape how a back injury develops and what it means for recovery. Some injuries remain confined to soft tissue, while others carry lasting consequences that extend into daily functioning and legal recourse. Denver residents recovering from a fall should weigh each of these factors carefully, since they often determine both the medical path forward and the strength of any legal claim.
Severity Varies

The severity of back injuries caused by falls can vary widely, from mild sprains to significant spinal cord damage. The force of the impact and its location along the spine both influence the outcome.
Seek Medical Attention
Medical care after any fall is important, especially when symptoms such as back pain, numbness, or weakness are present. These signs might indicate a more serious injury that needs attention.
Hidden Symptoms
Shock, adrenaline, or embarrassment after a fall might mask signs of injury. Pain, stiffness, or mobility issues can appear hours or days later.
Catastrophic Injuries

Spinal cord injuries are classified as catastrophic and often lead to long-lasting changes in daily life. They typically require ongoing medical care and can significantly reduce a person’s overall well-being.
Legal Considerations
When another party’s negligence caused the fall, the resulting back injury may support a legal claim. Documenting the
symptoms to look for after a fall on the back
as they appear, along with when they started, gives that claim a stronger factual foundation.
When to Seek Medical Attention

Delaying medical treatment can lead to long-term consequences. While minor back discomfort may resolve on its own, other injuries, such as fractures or disc damage, can worsen without proper care. Symptoms that progress over time, such as increasing weakness, spreading tingling, or pain that disrupts sleep or daily function, warrant a visit to the doctor. Denver offers wide access to orthopedic specialists and imaging services, so there is little reason to delay. Early diagnosis provides a clearer understanding of the injury and helps guide treatment, whether physical therapy or more advanced intervention. Documentation from initial and follow-up appointments can also serve as valuable evidence in a legal claim.

Back injuries are not always apparent right away. Persistent pain, numbness, tingling, or reduced range of motion should prompt a visit to a medical provider, since diagnostic tools like X-rays or MRIs can reveal internal injuries that are not visible on the surface. Prompt treatment can help prevent complications and support recovery.
Things to Do at the Accident Scene

If you fall in a public or private space, try to document the conditions that caused your fall. Take photos, gather witness contact information, and file an incident report. Do not brush off the incident; what seems minor initially could become a serious health and legal matter.
Things to Do After Leaving the Accident Scene

Once you have left the scene, seek medical attention, even if you feel fine. Keep copies of all medical records, prescriptions, and follow-up instructions. Avoid posting about the fall on social media, and consult a personal injury attorney before making any formal statements to third parties.
What Types of Compensation Can You Get for Your Back Injury?
Depending on the circumstances of your case, you may be entitled to
compensation

for medical bills, therapy, lost wages, and pain and suffering. In cases involving especially reckless or malicious conduct, Colorado law also permits injured individuals to pursue exemplary damages. A qualified attorney can help you assess what types of compensation might apply to your case.
